family: rows of blocks of 1s rewritten by two sweeps (parity and mod 4 structure, chaotic)
summary: The Pascal machine (1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF) in a mirror, started in state D: bounces write rows of Pascal's triangle mod 2, and in Lean it halts only if that machine's list program fails from another start; open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now the Pascal machine's question. This table is the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in a mirror, started in state D: every bounce writes the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2, an odd frozen block halts, and the machine never halts if that machine's list program never fails from EO [b, a, b, a, a, a] none 0 (all Lean, kernel). The list program ran 40,000 steps from there without failing.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 62,751 cells have been visited and 51,067 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L A> 1^n R reaches L 1^n A> R; L 1^n C> 1 R reaches L C> 1 1^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: No periodic structure, no cellular-automaton rule
claims.text: Up to 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps the tape has no long periodic stretch, and no sliding-block code of radius up to 7 (with any fixed shift) maps the tape at one visit of the right end to the next on the last 400 sweeps.

claims.title: The four block rules
claims.text: For all block sizes and every tape around them: C passes a single 1 (x 1 0 1 0 1^c <C becomes x <C 1 1 0 1^(c+2)); C bounces off a block of two or more (1 1 0 1^c <C becomes 0 1 1 A> 1^(c+1)); A shreds an odd block into single 1s (A> 1^a 0 1^(2k+1) 0 becomes 1^(a+1) 0 (1 0)^k 1 A>); A turns round at an even block.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: C, going left over a block of 1s onto a 0 that has 1 0 on its left, brings the machine to E reading a 1, the halting transition. By the transition table this is the only way to halt: E is entered only from D reading 0, and D only from C reading 0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps, and no near miss
claims.text: Direct simulation: C reads a 0 1,250,049,447 times and bounces 208,505 times; the smallest block bounced off, other than the leftmost, has 3 cells (a block of 2 would make the halting pattern). D reads a 0 only 56 times, each time on the blank cell left of the whole tape.

claims.title: A structure mod 4
claims.text: At 50,072 sampled moments when C reads a 0 in the first 4·10<sup>6</sup> steps, 5,365,538 of the 5,366,200 blocks right of the head (not counting the first and the last) have length 3 mod 4. Left of the head, an even block other than the leftmost has length 0 mod 4 and is followed by an odd number of single 1s.

claims.title: The run stays in a small set of rows
claims.text: Changing one far block of the tape at step 3·10<sup>5</sup> by 2, 4 or 8 cells, or adding or deleting single 1s, never led to a halt in 6·10<sup>5</sup> more steps (30 trials each); adding 1 or 3 cells to a block left of the head led to a halt in 16 of 30 trials. Random rows of odd blocks halt quickly in more than half of the trials.

claims.title: No proof by window automata
claims.text: Closed position sets and finite automata reduction with automata that remember the last 2 to 8 runs of a side by length class (exact, then mod 2 or mod 4), the parity of runs of single 1s and flags for even blocks further out find no certificate.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct C simulator on blocks of 16 cells (a full table for every block, state and side of entry; checked against tools/c/tmrun.c: the same number of 1s on the tape after 3·108 steps) runs 1012 steps from blank tape without a halt; the tape is then about 1.9 million cells long.

claims.title: The Pascal machine in a mirror
claims.text: This table is the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF read in a mirror, with that machine's states A to F renamed D, E, F, A, B, C. The blank tape is its own mirror image, so the run from blank tape is, cell for cell in the mirror, the run of the Pascal table started in state D, and this machine halts if and only if that run halts.

claims.title: One bounce is one row of Pascal's triangle mod 2
claims.text: Every theorem of the Pascal machine's folder holds here with left and right exchanged; its Lean files are compiled here unchanged (lean/P75625/). At a left turn in B, with the zone right of the head a word in the 4-cell letters 0111 and 1111 and the frozen tape 1 1 1 ... left of it, one bounce turns the zone into the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2 (closed form by Lucas' theorem), and takes two cells from the frozen block. A frozen block of odd length followed by 0 1 halts, whatever the zone, clean or walled (the halt: C reading 0 with 1 0 to its left).

claims.title: The holdout is the Pascal machine's list program, from another start
claims.text: The first left turn in B, at step 46, is the list state EO [b, a, b, a, a, a] none 0 of the Pascal machine's list machine arun (zone b a b a a a). If that list machine never fails from there, this machine never halts. The Pascal machine's own run starts it at EO [b, a] none 1.

claims.title: Where the list machine can fail
claims.text: For every state: a turn with no lone 1 in the zone never fails; a crossing turn with a clean far part whose tape ends in a single 1 never fails, and plain and crossing turns ending in a single 1 hand that on. So the list machine fails only at a crossing turn with blank end, at an EO turn during a crossing, or at a crossing turn whose far part is not clean.

claims.title: The list machine from this start: 40,000 steps
claims.text: Run on its own, 40,000 list steps without a failure (zone up to 19,162 letters, every far part clean). The 2,343 crossing turns with blank end all follow one of four early EO turns during a crossing (the last after list step 4,552); 2,339 have a witness, and the other 4 (frozen word 0) are passed. In lockstep with the real machine the list machine agrees at all 20,967 right turns of the first 2·108 steps.
claims.where: py/mirror_run.py of the folder of 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB (run D 40000, lockstep D 2e8)

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly if the Pascal table started in D halts (Lean), and it never halts if the Pascal machine's list machine never fails from EO [b, a, b, a, a, a] none 0 (Lean). Whether it fails is the same open question as for the Pascal machine, from another start.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: C with 1 two left, 0 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 3 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..7; n = 8 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine's tape is a long row of blocks of 1s with single 0s between them. The head sweeps left and right over the row and rewrites it by four simple rules, and the machine stops only if one of the sweeps meets a block of exactly two 1s in the wrong place.

facts.text: The Pascal machine's table read in a mirror, started in state D.
Each bounce writes the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2.
Steps of the list program from this start, without a failure.

sections.heading: Two sweeps, four rules
html: Read the tape as a row of blocks of 1s with a single 0 between neighbours, for example 5 1 9 1 1 1 5 for 11111 0 1 0 111111111 0 1 0 1 0 1 0 11111. The head only ever does two things.
Sweeping left (state C) it wants every second block to be a single 1. It deletes that single 1 and gives one cell to the block on each side, so a block between two single 1s grows by 2:

<svg viewBox="0 0 560 150" role="img" aria-label="the left sweep turns the row 5 1 9 1 7 into 7 11 and so on" style="width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:13px var(--mono)"><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><rect x="20" y="20" width="70" height="26" rx="4"/><rect x="100" y="20" width="22" height="26" rx="4" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><rect x="132" y="20" width="118" height="26" rx="4"/><rect x="260" y="20" width="22" height="26" rx="4" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><rect x="292" y="20" width="94" height="26" rx="4"/><rect x="20" y="100" width="94" height="26" rx="4"/><rect x="124" y="100" width="142" height="26" rx="4"/><rect x="276" y="100" width="110" height="26" rx="4"/><path d="M111 50 L 111 92 M 271 50 L 271 92" stroke-dasharray="2 4"/></g><g fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle"><text x="55" y="38">5</text><text x="111" y="38">1</text><text x="191" y="38">9</text><text x="271" y="38">1</text><text x="339" y="38">7</text><text x="67" y="118">6</text><text x="195" y="118">11</text><text x="331" y="118">8</text><text x="470" y="38">before</text><text x="470" y="118">after the sweep</text><text x="200" y="76">each single 1 is shared out between its neighbours</text></g></svg>
When the block in a "single" place has two or more 1s, the head takes two cells off it and turns round (a bounce).

Sweeping right (state A) it treats the blocks in turn: one block is shredded, the next is kept and grows by 2, the next is shredded, and so on. Shredding a block of 2k+1 cells leaves k single 1s. A block of even length in a shredding place turns the head round.

All four rules are proved in Lean for every block size. They explain the shapes on the tape: blocks of length 3, 7, 11, ... shred into an odd number of single 1s, and that keeps the next sweep to the left in step with the row. In the run, 99.99% of the blocks to the right of the head have such a length.

The only way to stop. The machine halts exactly when the sweep to the left finds two 0s side by side with a 1 beyond them. Two 0s side by side arise in one way: a bounce off a block of exactly two 1s. At the very left end of the tape that is harmless, anywhere else it is fatal. In 20 billion steps the head bounced 208,505 times and the smallest block it bounced off inside the row had three cells.

Is that luck? A test says no: change one block far from the head by one cell (so that its length becomes even), and the machine halts in about half of the trials. Change it by two or four cells and nothing happens. The row from blank tape obeys a hidden rule about odd and even lengths, and probably one about lengths mod 4. Finding that rule exactly, in a form a proof checker accepts, is what is missing. Two automatic searches for it (closed sets of tapes described by small automata) found nothing.

sections.heading: The Pascal machine, in a mirror
html: Read the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in a mirror and rename its states A to F as D, E, F, A, B, C: you get this machine's table exactly. The blank tape looks the same in a mirror, so this machine's run is that machine's table started in state D, seen in a mirror. Lean checks the correspondence, and every theorem about that table comes over with left and right exchanged.

So the picture of that machine applies. A zone next to the growing right end is a word in the 4-cell letters 0111 and 1111. Each time the head turns left in B, one bounce sweeps the zone and replaces it by its running parity, the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2: the nested triangles in the space-time diagram above. Each bounce takes two cells from the frozen block left of the head. A frozen block of odd length followed by 0 1 would halt the machine, whatever the zone.

After 46 steps the run is in a state of the Pascal machine's list program, which follows the machine from turn to turn using lists alone. Lean proves that if this program never fails from EO [b, a, b, a, a, a] none 0, the machine never halts. It ran 40,000 list steps from there without failing. Lean also proves the program can fail in only three ways.

sections.heading: Odd blocks, single gaps
html: Stop the simulator after the first few steps: every run of 0s inside the tape is a single 0 and every block of 1s has odd length, except for at most one or two runs (in 27 snapshots up to 109 steps), presumably where the sweep is at work. At step 109 there are 11,687 blocks:

length13579111315
blocks5,0582,4431,2971,128431487163261

The head sweeps across the whole tape and crosses each block with a simple shift rule (proved in Lean for every length), so all the changes happen at the single 0s between blocks. How a sweep transforms the list is the next thing to find; for now the order of the blocks looks disordered. The halt (state E reading a 1) needs a particular local pattern the sweeps have never produced.

sections.heading: Each sweep rewrites the whole tape
html: After 3·108 steps the tape is 33,829 cells of odd blocks of 1s split by single 0s, and it has no long repeated stretch anywhere. Every sweep of the head changes the whole of it, and not in a local way: no rule that computes each new cell from a window of up to 15 old cells explains the change. Information travels along the tape during a sweep, as when a number is multiplied digit by digit with carries. Finding that arithmetic is the next step.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).
After 109 steps the tape spans 62,751 cells (166 left of the start, 42,569 right), with a density of 1s of 0.814.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
